name: AGILE
summary: Italian multipurpose high-energy astronomy satellite conducting X-ray and gamma-ray observations from 2007 to 2024. Its original team science white paper identified deep Andromeda exposures testing dark-matter models as an objective. This primary-source objective is retained without equating generic gamma-ray observations with published dark-matter limits.
physics_targets: Gamma radiation from dark-matter-rich objects, an original science objective
Testing dark-matter models in Andromeda; objective, with no independent result verified
detection_principle: GRID's silicon tracker reconstructs electron–positron pairs from gamma conversion, with a minicalorimeter and anticoincidence system measuring events and rejecting charged-particle backgrounds. SuperAGILE simultaneously images hard X-rays. Dark-matter tests require models of target gamma radiation and astrophysical backgrounds.

status.label: Scientific data taking ended; data archived
status.evidence: AGILE team GCN 35726 explicitly states that science observations stopped on 2024-01-18 and reentry occurred on 2024-02-14.

timeline.event: The team's science document listed deep Andromeda exposures testing dark-matter models as an objective.
Launched from Sriharikota, India, into a low-background equatorial orbit.
Reentered the atmosphere after natural orbital decay.

results.summary: The original science-objective document explicitly supports a dark-matter research scope. No dedicated published AGILE-data dark-matter-limit paper was verified in this search, so no invented cross-section limit is supplied.
The end-of-mission announcement confirms that science archives and catalogs are available to researchers; this does not establish a dark-matter discovery.

science_scope: Multipurpose gamma-ray astronomy mission included on the basis of the collaboration's primary science objectives, not a generic community-catalog label. Specific AGILE dark-matter search results remain unverified; its presentation should identify a confirmed dark-matter science objective with dedicated results pending, distinguished from projects with published particle-dark-matter limits.
